text:
rowan: FYI I just opened a PR to add concrete examples for audit log exports and retention guidance. Need quick eyes on SOC2 phrasing.
jess: paste curl/python snippets? I want to check SDK parity.
rowan: curl:
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export?tenant=contoso&retain=30d&redact=true" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{\"format\":\"ndjson\",\"since\":\"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z\"}'

rowan: python:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client=RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp=client.audit.export(tenant_id='contoso', retain='30d', redact=True, format='ndjson', since='2026-03-01T00:00:00Z')
if resp.status_code==200: print(resp.download_url)

omar: Security/legal notes: 1) Use neutral SOC2 wording: "Example uses 30 days; configure retention per your policy." 2) Call out export TTL (24h) and that access is logged. 3) Redaction caveat: server-side redaction may remove PII but can affect forensic completeness.
rowan: I'll change text to match and add a small JSON example for redaction_policy: { \"redaction_policy\": \"pii-only\" } plus one-liners for pii-only/full/none.
docbot: automated-check: link-check failed for https://docs.redwood.ai/export-guides (404)
jess: sgtm from SDK after the policy snippet and status check.
omar: sgtm security; I'll run a quick sweep for any overclaims about SOC2 scope once updated.
rowan: thanks all, updating PR now and will request reviews once pushed.
